title: Stable pointed curves and normalized component special points
statement: Let $f:W\to T$ be a morphism of schemes and let $s_i:T\to W$ for $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be sections, where $n\geq0$. A stable pointed curve is a projective-bundle morphism [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with connected nonempty nodal geometric fibres [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres] that are reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and of pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension]. The sections are disjoint and lie in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-field] and geometric point $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, form the geometric fibre $C=W\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For each irreducible component, take its reduced induced scheme and canonical normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], and the canonical map $\nu_Z:\widetilde C_Z\to C$. Define its genus by [def-pc-genus], using the induced $\Omega$-structure. The special points on $\widetilde C_Z$ are the inverse image under $\nu_Z$ of the nonsmooth points of $C$ or the images of the base-changed sections. If the genus is zero this set has at least three points; if the genus is one it has at least one point. Markings are labelled in this predicate; allowing permutation in an isomorphism gives the unordered convention. The canonical component normalization map and its genus are included in this definition.
